results.title: Scaffold, manifest format, and repo-shape helpers
results.summary: Built the Pitwall phase-1 substrate TDD-style: a capped `key: value` frontmatter parser that throws on lists/indents/block scalars/duplicate keys, a provider-manifest loader with two declarative detectors (glob + exit code, both must pass when both present), git repo-shape helpers porting the `gwt` sibling-path convention (zero-commit- and submodule-safe), a never-throwing `openspec` capability probe, and a composable temp-repo test fixture — 79 tests, all green, zero dependencies, no build step. Note: `node --test tests/` fails on Node 26 (a bare directory positional is no longer expanded), so `tests/index.js` was added as a documented entry shim to keep the spec's validation command working on both Node 22 and 26; also, the repo has zero commits, so `git diff HEAD` errors — the review diff must be read via `git diff` (all files are intent-to-add). Forward risk for phase 2: its planned `ideate` manifest has no `doneWhen*` key, which this loader rejects by design per the phase-1 spec. — Phase 1 is implemented faithfully: no build step, zero runtime dependencies, `node --test` as the harness, the capped frontmatter parser that throws on lists/nesting/block scalars/duplicate keys, the provider loader with required-key + missing-detector + duplicate-stage rejection, the repo helpers, and the never-throwing openspec probe. The `resolveWorktreePath` derivation matches the cited `gwt` pattern exactly (`${dirname}/${basename}-${branch//\\//-}`, git.zsh:279), and every "Key test case" the spec names — literal `---` in the body, `feat/a/b` flattening, zero-commit repos, submodule exclusion, stubbed openspec — has a corresponding assertion. No critical or high findings; the ten items are hardening and documentation (undeclared `tests/index.js`, the shell-exec trust boundary of `doneWhenCmd`, and an unpruned `**` walk being the notable three). Ready to commit. Caveat: per the reviewer's git-only Bash restriction I did not execute `node --test tests/`, so the suite's green status is asserted from reading, not from a run.

results.title: Stage inference core
results.summary: Implemented the stage-inference core: the fixed seven-beat model (src/beats.js) with wrapper-owned worktree/cleanup detectors, resolveBeat's ordered walk with completed/skipped/warnings/branch/changeId (src/inference.js), dual-source execute progress with openspec-CLI-first and a fence-aware tasks.md fallback (src/progress.js), changeStatus on src/openspec.js, five provider manifests, seven beat fixtures, and 38 new tests. Both spec validation commands pass (117 tests, 0 fail). — All ten cycle-1 findings are fixed: `resolveBeat` now anchors on `superprojectRoot` (walked to the outermost superproject) and warns, with a submodule case in the test suite; `openspec-execute.md` carries `effort: high`; `skipped` excludes the current beat and the two contradicting spec lines were reconciled; `providerIsDone` delegates to `evaluateProvider`; the all-seven-complete terminal state, the CLI-change-id adoption, the `openspecAvailable` split, the narrowed "never throws" doc, the `cleanupIsDone` convention caveat, and the alphabetical `tests/index.js` import are all in place. What remains is five non-blocking items — chiefly a divergence between the execute manifest's grep detector and `progress.js`'s fence-stripping counter, and the untested nested-submodule walk that the cycle-1 fix introduced. Verdict: PASS, ready to commit.
findings: medium/logic /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/providers/openspec-execute.md:7 — the execute detector and the progress counter disagree about what a task checkbox is. `grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[-*+] \[ \]'` scans the raw file, so an example `- [ ]` inside a fenced block in `tasks.md` keeps the beat incomplete forever (spec-phase-2.md:193's hard-stall mode) while `countTasks` at src/progress.js:48 strips fences and reports `3 of 3` — the baton would print 'beat: execute, 3 of 3'. The separators also differ: the grep demands exactly one space after the bullet, while CHECKBOX at src/progress.js:12 allows `[ \t]+`, so `-  [ ] task` reads as done to the detector and as incomplete to the counter. → Make the manifest detector agree with the counter — either widen the pattern to `[-*+][[:space:]]+\[ \]` and accept the fenced-block gap in a manifest comment, or drop `doneWhenCmd` in favour of a detector that shells out to the same counting code.

medium/testing /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/src/repo.js:99 — `superprojectRoot`'s defining behaviour is untested. tests/inference.test.js:223 builds a single-hop submodule, which a one-line `rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` would pass identically; the walk-to-the-outermost loop and `MAX_SUBMODULE_DEPTH` are what spec-phase-2.md:194 actually specifies ('walked to the outermost one') and nothing exercises them. `worktreeRoot` and `isMerged` are likewise new exports with no case in tests/repo.test.js (describe blocks stop at `inWorktree`/`probeOpenspec`). → Add a nested-submodule case (`addSubmodule` twice) asserting the anchor is the outermost tree, and direct `superprojectRoot`/`worktreeRoot`/`isMerged` describes to tests/repo.test.js alongside the phase-1 exports they sit with.

The builder already edited this spec this cycle to reconcile the `skipped` wording and tick the Open Item, so the table is the one part left stale. → Add the three files and their one-line changes to the Modified Files table.

low/spec-deviation /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/docs/ideation/pitwall/spec-phase-2.md:186 — the Manual Testing item ('Run `resolveBeat` against this very repo and confirm it reports the `specs` beat') is false as written from the main checkout: this repo is on `main` with no `pitwall-main` sibling, so `worktreeIsDone` fails and the walk stops at `worktree` with `completed: ['ideate','refine','contract']`. It only reports `specs` from inside the feature worktree. → Either qualify the item ('run from the feature worktree') or restate the expected beat, then tick it.

low/pattern-mismatch /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/src/providers.js:168 — the cycle-1 collapse of `providerIsDone` into `evaluateProvider` moved the same problem onto `detectCmd`: `src/` now calls `runDetector` directly everywhere, so the exported `detectCmd` is kept alive only by tests/providers.test.js:138-155, exactly the 'dead in src/, alive in tests' shape the prior finding objected to. → Either drop `detectCmd` and retarget its four assertions at `providerIsDone({doneWhenCmd: ...})`, or state in its doc comment that it is a public helper retained for callers outside this module.

results.title: Baton command and gitignore preflight
results.summary: Implemented phase 3: the pure `renderBaton` renderer (src/baton.js) with golden files for all seven beats plus the all-complete state, the three-outcome `git check-ignore` preflight with glob de-globbing and nested-prefix collapsing (src/preflight.js), and the `pw next` CLI with `--json`, `--help`, and an exit-2 no-git pre-check (src/cli.js), wired to a thin `commands/next.md` slash command. Full suite is green at 176 tests / 0 fail (baseline was 122) and all four spec validation commands pass. — Every blocking item from cycle 1 is fixed: tests/cli.test.js now exists and is registered in tests/index.js, covering exit 0 with byte-exact golden output, one-line no-git guidance on exit 2 with an explicit no-stack-trace assertion, parseable --json, unknown command and unknown `next` option, `--help` after the subcommand, and — the load-bearing case — `IGNORED BY GIT` still reported when run from a subdirectory, which is what proves the preflight is anchored at the repo root; `deglob` now adds the directory slash unless the final segment looks like a file, and the two tests that pinned the old miss are converted into passing cases; `BUILTIN_PROVIDERS` is documented in the spec's Modified Files table; and `commands/next.md` no longer falls back to the operator's cwd. Remaining findings are all non-blocking: one medium where the fixed slash-command guard now runs a shell construct its own `allowed-tools` list does not permit, plus four low-severity consistency and documentation nits. I did not execute the suites (tool restriction limits Bash to git commands), so the verdict rests on reading the diff, the fixtures, and the golden files — the implementation matches the spec's technical approach and is ready to commit once the `allowed-tools` mismatch is settled.
findings: medium/logic commands/next.md:19 — Regression from the cycle-1 fix: the `:-.` fallback is correctly gone, but the replacement runs `if [ -f "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}/src/cli.js" ]; then node ...; else echo ...; fi` while the frontmatter still declares `allowed-tools: Bash(node:*), Bash(test:*), Bash(echo:*)` (next.md:3). Nothing in that allow-list matches a command whose first word is `if` and whose predicate is `[`, so the one shell invocation the slash command exists to make is the one the frontmatter does not permit — the operator gets a permission prompt (or, non-interactively, no block at all) instead of the verbatim baton the Task section promises. The stale `Bash(test:*)` entry suggests the guard was originally written with `test -f`. → Rewrite the invocation as prefix-matchable segments, e.g. `test -f "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/src/cli.js" && node "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/src/cli.js" next || echo "pitwall: …"`, so each segment matches a declared `Bash(...)` prefix; or drop `Bash(test:*)` and declare whatever the final form actually runs.

low/logic src/baton.js:101 — `HANDOFF_LINES[provider.handoff] ?? provider.handoff ?? DEFAULT_HANDOFF` looks up a manifest-supplied string on a plain object literal, so a manifest declaring `handoff: constructor` (or `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`) resolves to an inherited `Object.prototype` member and renders a function body into the baton instead of the value verbatim — the exact opposite of the spec's rule that "Anything else is rendered verbatim". src/cli.js:66 already guards this class of bug deliberately ("as a Map so a bare `constructor` on the command line resolves to nothing"); baton.js does not follow its own convention. → Make HANDOFF_LINES a `Map` (or use `Object.hasOwn`/`Object.create(null)`) and add a baton test asserting `handoff: constructor` renders as the literal text `constructor`.

low/pattern-mismatch tests/cli.test.js:23 — The `isolated()` git-env guard is duplicated verbatim in tests/cli.test.js:23-35 and tests/preflight-gitignore.test.js:24-36, while every other shared fixture concern (`withPath`, `pathWithout`, `git`, `tempRoot`) lives once in tests/helpers/repo-fixture.js — which already sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` for its own subprocesses (repo-fixture.js:9-17). Two copies will drift the first time a third env var needs neutralising. → Move `isolated()` into tests/helpers/repo-fixture.js beside `withPath` and import it from both suites.

low/spec-deviation src/preflight.js:4 — The module's public surface is wider than the spec's snippet: `Preflight` is `{ignored, warnings}` where the spec declares `{ignored:string[]}`, and `artifactPaths(providers)` is a second export the File Changes table only describes as `checkIgnored(cwd, paths)`. Both are well-reasoned and documented in place (the three-outcome argument at preflight.js:4-7 is right, and deriving paths from manifests is what makes a swapped provider bring its own artifact directory), but phase 5 consumes this module and the spec it will be written against does not describe this shape. → Record the widened `Preflight` shape and the `artifactPaths` export in the phase handoff notes or the phase-5 spec so the next phase codes against the real interface.

low/performance src/cli.js:49 — `next()` resolves the repository root with `worktreeRoot(superprojectRoot(cwd) ?? cwd)` and then hands `cwd` to `resolveBeat`, which immediately repeats both queries at inference.js:67-73 — four extra `git` spawns per `pw next`, and two sources of truth for the anchor if either ever changes. → Either accept the duplication with a comment (the no-git check must precede `resolveBeat`, which never throws), or have `resolveBeat` accept/return the resolved root so the CLI reuses it.

results.title: Worktree beat
results.summary: Phase 4 ships `pw start`: a new `src/worktree.js` (`startWorktree` + `isInside` + a `WorktreeError` tier for the first mutating git calls in `src/`), the `start` subcommand in `src/cli.js` (which resolves the post-create baton from the *new* worktree, prints the `cd` line around a pure `renderBaton`, and exits 2 with a remedy on failure), a `stage: worktree` manifest, and the `/pitwall:start` slash command. Guards cover idempotence, the inside-the-target no-op, prunable/occupied paths, branch-already-checked-out (including the main checkout), invalid and flag-shaped branch names, unborn HEAD (explicit pre-check, since `git worktree add` silently creates an orphan instead of failing), and unresolvable bases (`origin/<default>` verified, `HEAD` with no fetch when there is no remote). Full suite went 188 → 215 tests, 0 failures; both manual test cases were run against a scratch clone. — Phase 4 lands cleanly: `startWorktree` is a faithful port of `gwt` (/Users/tinetti/tinetti_dev_tools/files/zsh/git.zsh:267-288) with the three added properties the spec demanded — idempotence, the inside-the-target no-op, and the remote-less `HEAD` fallback with the fetch skipped — plus the explicit unborn-HEAD and unset-`origin/HEAD` guards, each carrying an operator-facing remedy. Path derivation is correctly consumed from phase 1's `resolveWorktreePath` rather than re-derived, the `start` subcommand re-runs inference from the *new* tree so the baton names the beat that follows, and `providers/pitwall-worktree.md` supplies the baton while detection stays wrapper-owned in `beats.js`. Test coverage exceeds the spec's list (every required case plus prunable-worktree, occupied-directory, branch-already-checked-out and invalid-name cases), goldens and `tests/index.js` were updated consistently, and no critical or high findings remain — ready to commit; the four notes above are polish, with the `$ARGUMENTS` quoting rationale in commands/start.md worth correcting before phase 5 packages the plugin.
findings: medium/security /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/commands/start.md:26 — `$ARGUMENTS` is interpolated into the `!` bash line inside double quotes, and the comment at line 17 justifies it as safe because "the argument is quoted". Double quotes do not suppress `$(...)` or backticks, so `/pitwall:start feat/x$(...)` executes inside the already-approved command string, and the `allowed-tools` prefix match cannot gate a substitution nested in a command that already matched → Either correct the rationale to state the real residual risk, or stop interpolating: emit the branch through a mechanism the shell does not re-expand (e.g. pass it via the environment set outside the interpolation, or have the CLI read it from stdin) before the plugin ships in phase 5.

low/spec-deviation /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/src/worktree.js:8 — Spec's declared interface is `{path, created, branchCreated, base:string}`; the implementation widens `base` to `string|null` and returns `null` for every no-op/existing-branch path. The reasoning in the typedef is sound (naming a base nobody chose would be an invention), but it is an undeclared change to a spec-stated signature → Note the widening in the spec (or contract addendum) so phase 5's consumers are not written against `base:string`.

low/logic /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/src/worktree.js:233 — The unborn-HEAD guard runs after the "branch already checked out" guard, and `git worktree list --porcelain` still prints `branch refs/heads/<name>` for an unborn HEAD. `pw start main` in a fresh `git init` therefore reports "already checked out at …" instead of the specified "no commits yet — make an initial commit first" remedy (spec Failure Modes, unborn HEAD row) → Hoist the `rev-parse --verify HEAD` check above the `elsewhere` lookup so the zero-commit remedy always wins.

low/spec-deviation /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/src/cli.js:20 — The shared USAGE block advertises `--json` as a global option, but `start` rejects every flag with exit 2 (`start` at line 103), so `pw start --json` prints a usage message that lists an option the subcommand refuses → Scope the Options line to `next` (e.g. `--json  (next) Print the raw inference result…`) so the usage text is not self-contradicting.

results.title: Cleanup baton, packaging, and adoption
results.summary: Phase 5 built: the cleanup baton (providers/pitwall-cleanup.md), pw status and /pitwall:status via a new renderPosition export, plugin packaging (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, executable bin/pw, package.json bin), the four vendored /spec:* routing commands copied byte-identically, README.md, and tests/commands.test.js. Three spec items needed decisions: the superpowers manifest ships at examples/superpowers-execute.md (inside providers/ it makes loadProviders throw "duplicate stage execute" and breaks every command); plugin.json declares no commands key (no precedent among 79 installed plugins, and the key is additive to convention discovery so it would double-register) with the declared set living in tests/commands.test.js instead; and a new optional manifest key "argument" (change-id | branch | none) stops the cleanup baton rendering "/mar CHANGE-ID" — it now renders "/mar feat/thing". All 249 tests pass. — All eight cycle-1 findings are resolved: the real install check was performed and its result is now load-bearing in both the spec (Adoption key decision at spec-phase-5.md:125-126, plus a four-row deviation table at :196-201) and README.md's Install section, which correctly states the plugin ships `/pitwall:spec:*` and that the bare `/spec:*` names the OpenSpec batons use come from the `~/.claude/commands/spec/` symlinks; the three medium spec-deviations are recorded in the contract; ARGUMENT_SOURCES is now a Map with a DEFAULT_ARGUMENT fallback (src/baton.js:27-31, :118-120); `bin/pw --help` is spawned and asserted (tests/commands.test.js:270-281); the examples/ swap is loaded and rendered in a scratch providers dir; and README.md:109 now names all three warning surfaces. Zero critical and zero high findings remain — the three below are non-blocking. The implementation is ready to commit; the outstanding medium is one sentence of manifest prose the spec asked for and the README currently carries instead.
findings: medium/spec-deviation /Users/tinetti/Projects/pitwall/providers/openspec-specs.md:8 — Spec *Adoption* key decision (spec-phase-5.md:127) and the Failure Modes row "Vendored spec commands | Broken layer" (spec-phase-5.md:169) both require that "the OpenSpec provider manifest must state which artifact it assumes — the `/spec:*` command, the `opsx:*` skill, or the `openspec` CLI directly". Neither providers/openspec-specs.md nor providers/openspec-execute.md says so; the only place the `opsx:*` layer is named is README.md:105, and the vendored commands' own `openspec init` guard (commands/spec/propose.md:9) covers the missing-directory case but not the stated mitigation. Non-blocking because the operator-facing message exists, but the mitigation is not where the spec put it → Add one sentence to the body of providers/openspec-specs.md and providers/openspec-execute.md naming the layer each assumes (the `/spec:*` command, which invokes the per-project `opsx:*` skill), or record the relocation to README.md:105 in the spec's deviation table.

It is benign and consistent with the Rollout prerequisite to create `github.com/tinetti/pitwall`, but the spec presents that block as the file's contents and the deviation table records every other divergence → Add `homepage` to the spec's JSON snippet so the block still reads as the shipped file.

The property is now covered indirectly — tests/commands.test.js:200-240 loads and renders the swap, and tests/provider-swap.test.js asserts a rebind needs no source change — but the one-file diff itself was never observed → Run the `cp examples/superpowers-execute.md providers/openspec-execute.md` swap once, confirm `git status --porcelain` reports one file, revert, and tick the box.
